<a id="c-01"></a>
## C-01. Backtrader mental model

Backtrader is an event-driven engine built around **lines**. Data feeds, indicators, observers, and strategies expose time-indexed line buffers. Indicators are normally declared once in `__init__`; Backtrader calculates their dependency graph and calls strategy methods as data becomes available.

The central objects are:

| Object | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `bt.Cerebro` | Coordinates feeds, strategies, broker, analyzers, optimization, and execution |
| `bt.feeds.*` | Maps external data into standard or custom lines |
| `bt.Strategy` | Holds indicator graph and event/order logic |
| `bt.Indicator` | Produces one or more lines from data/other lines |
| `BackBroker` | Simulates cash, positions, orders, fills, commission, and slippage |
| `bt.Sizer` | Determines order size when strategy does not pass one |
| `bt.Analyzer` | Computes results without becoming a plotted line |
| `bt.Observer` | Tracks values as lines, commonly for plotting |

Canonical lifecycle:

```text
construct feeds and Cerebro
instantiate Strategy and indicators
preload/run indicator minimum periods
Strategy.prenext() while not all minimum periods are ready
Strategy.nextstart() once at the first fully ready bar
Strategy.next() for subsequent bars
broker sends notify_order / notify_trade callbacks
Strategy.stop() after simulation
```

An order created inside ordinary `next()` after observing bar `t` is not eligible to execute earlier on bar `t`. A market order normally fills at the next available bar’s open.

<a id="c-02"></a>
## C-02. Imports, capability checks, and aliases

Use conventional imports:

```python
import backtrader as bt
import pandas as pd
```

`bt.ind` and `bt.indicators` refer to the same indicator namespace. Generated production code SHOULD use `bt.ind` for compactness or `bt.indicators` for clarity, but it MUST be consistent.

Inspect an indicator rather than guessing:

```python
import backtrader as bt


def describe_indicator(name: str) -> dict[str, object]:
    cls = getattr(bt.ind, name, None)
    if cls is None or not isinstance(cls, type) or not issubclass(cls, bt.Indicator):
        raise LookupError(f"No Backtrader indicator class: {name}")
    return {
        "class": f"{cls.__module__}.{cls.__name__}",
        "aliases_declared_by_class": tuple(getattr(cls, "alias", ())),
        "alias_of": getattr(cls, "aliased", "") or None,
        "lines": tuple(cls.lines.getlinealiases()),
        "params": dict(cls.params._getitems()),
    }


print(describe_indicator("MACDHisto"))
```

Important verified aliases:

| Concept | Preferred exact class | Useful aliases | Output lines |
|---|---|---|---|
| Simple moving average | `MovingAverageSimple` | `SMA`, `SimpleMovingAverage` | `sma` |
| Exponential moving average | `ExponentialMovingAverage` | `EMA`, `MovingAverageExponential` | `ema` |
| Wilder average | `SmoothedMovingAverage` | `SMMA`, `WilderMA`, `MovingAverageWilder` | `smma` |
| RSI | `RelativeStrengthIndex` | `RSI`, `RSI_SMMA`, `RSI_Wilder` | `rsi` |
| Safe RSI | `RSI_Safe` | - | `rsi` |
| ATR | `AverageTrueRange` | `ATR` | `atr` |
| True range | `TrueRange` | `TR` | `tr` |
| Standard deviation | `StandardDeviation` | `StdDev` | `stddev` |
| Bollinger Bands | `BollingerBands` | `BollingerBandsPct` is a different class | `mid`, `top`, `bot` |
| MACD | `MACD` | - | `macd`, `signal` |
| MACD histogram | `MACDHisto` | `MACDHistogram` | `macd`, `signal`, `histo` |
| Fast stochastic | `StochasticFast` | - | `percK`, `percD` |
| Slow stochastic | `Stochastic` | `StochasticSlow` | `percK`, `percD` |
| Full stochastic | `StochasticFull` | - | `percK`, `percD`, `percDSlow` |
| ADX | `AverageDirectionalMovementIndex` | `ADX` | `adx` |
| DMI | `DirectionalMovementIndex` | `DMI` | `adx`, `plusDI`, `minusDI` |
| Cross event | `CrossOver` | - | `crossover` |

Do not use `bt.ind.OBV`, `bt.ind.VWAP`, or `bt.ind.SuperTrend`; those names are not present in the Backtrader core package targeted by this manual.

The documented contrib study `Fractal` is a namespace exception:

```python
from backtrader.studies.contrib.fractal import Fractal
```

Do not generate `bt.ind.Fractal`; it is not exported there in `1.9.78.123`.

<a id="c-03"></a>
## C-03. The platform runner (what BacktestLoop does around your `Strategy` class)

**The strategy file contains ONLY the `Strategy` class (plus helpers).** The platform runner does everything a standalone script would do, so the strategy MUST NOT do any of it:

| Platform-owned step | What the runner does | What the strategy must NOT do |
|---|---|---|
| Data feeds | Injects every job feed (primary + `additionalSources`), each named `{SYMBOL}_{TIMEFRAME}` | No `bt.feeds.PandasData(...)`, no `cerebro.adddata`, no file/network reads |
| Cerebro | Constructs Cerebro, attaches the strategy, runs it | No `bt.Cerebro()`, no `cerebro.run()`, no `if __name__ == "__main__"` |
| Cash | `broker.setcash(start_cash)` from the job's initial-cash parameter | No `setcash` |
| Costs | `broker.setcommission(...)` from the platform **broker fee model** for the symbol's asset class (commission, margin, contract multiplier, stocklike flag) | No `setcommission`, no `set_slippage_*`, no invented fee numbers |
| Analyzers & results | Equity curve, Sharpe, returns, drawdown, trade list, order record - extracted into the platform result format shared with the VectorBT engine | No analyzers, no plotting, no result printing beyond diagnostic `print()` logs |
| Dates/symbols/timeframes | Job parameters | Never hardcoded in the strategy |

The authoring contract:

```python
import backtrader as bt


class Strategy(bt.Strategy):          # class name MUST be exactly "Strategy"
    # Required for live paper trading: declares that every piece of internal
    # state rebuilds from replaying recent bars (true for indicator-driven
    # logic - the standard case). Live deploys REFUSE strategies without it;
    # only genuinely path-dependent cross-restart state (counters spanning
    # restarts, running-PnL gates) uses live_resume_state() /
    # load_live_resume_state(state) hooks instead.
    live_resume_replay_safe = True

    params = dict(fast=10, slow=30)   # override-able via job params / experiments

    def __init__(self):
        self.fast = bt.ind.EMA(self.data.close, period=self.p.fast)
        self.slow = bt.ind.EMA(self.data.close, period=self.p.slow)
        self.cross = bt.ind.CrossOver(self.fast, self.slow)
        self.order = None

    def notify_order(self, order):
        if order.status in (order.Completed, order.Canceled, order.Margin, order.Rejected):
            self.order = None

    def next(self):
        if self.order:
            return
        if not self.position and self.cross[0] > 0:
            self.order = self.buy(size=1)
        elif self.position and self.cross[0] < 0:
            self.order = self.close()
```

Helper classes and functions MAY live in the same file, but the deliverable class the runner instantiates is the one named `Strategy`. `cheat_on_open` is not enabled by the runner - the standard event cycle (market orders fill at the next bar's open) always applies.

<a id="c-04"></a>
## C-04. Strategy lifecycle and standard order guard

A strategy that can have only one outstanding entry/exit order should use one pending-order reference:

```python
import backtrader as bt


class SingleOrderStrategy(bt.Strategy):
    params = dict(printlog=False)

    def __init__(self):
        self.pending_order: bt.Order | None = None

    def log(self, message: str) -> None:
        if self.p.printlog:
            timestamp = self.data.datetime.datetime(0).isoformat()
            print(f"{timestamp} {message}")

    def notify_order(self, order: bt.Order) -> None:
        if order.status in (order.Submitted, order.Accepted):
            return

        if order.status == order.Completed:
            side = "BUY" if order.isbuy() else "SELL"
            self.log(
                f"{side} filled price={order.executed.price:.6f} "
                f"size={order.executed.size:.6f} "
                f"commission={order.executed.comm:.6f}"
            )
        elif order.status in (order.Canceled, order.Margin, order.Rejected, order.Expired):
            self.log(f"Order failed: {order.getstatusname()}")

        if self.pending_order is not None and order.ref == self.pending_order.ref:
            self.pending_order = None
```

For bracket orders, multiple assets, scale-ins, or independent stop/target orders, a single variable is inadequate. Track orders by `order.ref` and role:

```python
self.orders: dict[int, str] = {}  # order.ref -> "entry" | "stop" | "target"
```

Never assume an order completed merely because `buy()` or `sell()` returned an object. Completion is reported through `notify_order`.

<a id="c-05"></a>
## C-05. Lines, indexing, and boolean expressions

### Inside `__init__`: build line expressions

```python
class LineGraphExample(bt.Strategy):
    def __init__(self):
        self.fast = bt.ind.EMA(self.data.close, period=10)
        self.slow = bt.ind.EMA(self.data.close, period=30)
        self.cross = bt.ind.CrossOver(self.fast, self.slow)
        self.previous_close_line = self.data.close(-1)
        self.valid_setup = bt.And(self.fast > self.slow, self.data.close > self.slow)
```

At this stage, `self.fast > self.slow` is a line operation, not one Boolean value. Python’s `and`, `or`, and ternary expression cannot represent the line graph. Use `bt.And`, `bt.Or`, `bt.If`, comparisons, and arithmetic.

Wrong:

```python
# WRONG in __init__: Python tries to coerce line objects to one truth value.
self.signal = (self.fast > self.slow) and (self.data.close > self.slow)
```

Correct:

```python
self.signal = bt.And(self.fast > self.slow, self.data.close > self.slow)
```

### Inside `next`: read concrete current/past values

```python
def next(self):
    current_close = float(self.data.close[0])
    previous_close = float(self.data.close[-1])
    current_fast = float(self.fast[0])
```

| Syntax | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `line[0]` | current value in `next` |
| `line[-1]` | previous value in `next` |
| `line[-n]` | `n` bars ago |
| `line(-1)` | delayed line object, normally created in `__init__` |
| `line[1]` | future buffer position; do not use for a historical decision |

An indicator instantiated without an explicit data argument inside a strategy generally receives the strategy’s first data automatically. Explicit input is still preferred in agent-generated code:

```python
self.rsi = bt.ind.RSI_Safe(self.data.close, period=14)
```

<a id="c-06"></a>
## C-06. Standard indicator implementations

### SMA

```python
sma = bt.ind.SMA(self.data.close, period=20)
value = sma.sma[0]
```

### Canonical EMA

Backtrader’s native EMA matches `BTL_CANONICAL_V1`: `alpha=2/(n+1)` with an initial arithmetic-average seed.

```python
ema = bt.ind.EMA(self.data.close, period=20)
value = ema.ema[0]
```

### Wilder RMA

```python
rma = bt.ind.SMMA(self.data.close, period=14)
value = rma.smma[0]
```

### Wilder RSI with safe division

Use `RSI_Safe`, not bare `RSI`, when flat data can occur. Bare `RSI` has `safediv=False` and may divide by zero.

```python
rsi = bt.ind.RSI_Safe(
    self.data.close,
    period=14,
    upperband=70.0,
    lowerband=30.0,
)
```

Variants:

```python
wilder_rsi = bt.ind.RSI_Wilder(self.data.close, period=14)
cutler_rsi = bt.ind.RSI_SMA(self.data.close, period=14)
ema_rsi = bt.ind.RSI_EMA(self.data.close, period=14)
```

These are different calculations. Do not substitute one for another.

### ATR

```python
atr = bt.ind.ATR(self.data, period=14)  # Wilder smoothing by default
```

To deliberately request another smoothing method:

```python
atr_sma = bt.ind.ATR(self.data, period=14, movav=bt.ind.SMA)
atr_ema = bt.ind.ATR(self.data, period=14, movav=bt.ind.EMA)
```

### Bollinger Bands

```python
bb = bt.ind.BollingerBands(
    self.data.close,
    period=20,
    devfactor=2.0,
    movav=bt.ind.SMA,
)
mid = bb.mid
upper = bb.top
lower = bb.bot
```

Backtrader’s standard deviation calculation uses the population form derived from rolling mean-of-squares minus squared mean.

### MACD

```python
macd = bt.ind.MACDHisto(
    self.data.close,
    period_me1=12,
    period_me2=26,
    period_signal=9,
    movav=bt.ind.EMA,
)
macd_line = macd.macd
signal_line = macd.signal
histogram = macd.histo
```

### Stochastic variants

```python
fast = bt.ind.StochasticFast(
    self.data,
    period=14,
    period_dfast=3,
    movav=bt.ind.SMA,
)
slow = bt.ind.Stochastic(
    self.data,
    period=14,
    period_dfast=3,
    period_dslow=3,
    movav=bt.ind.SMA,
)
full = bt.ind.StochasticFull(
    self.data,
    period=14,
    period_dfast=3,
    period_dslow=3,
    movav=bt.ind.SMA,
)
```

`Stochastic` is the slow version. Use `StochasticFast` to match VectorBT native `STOCH` under simple `%D` smoothing.

### ADX and DMI

```python
adx_only = bt.ind.ADX(self.data, period=14)
dmi = bt.ind.DMI(self.data, period=14)

adx_value = dmi.adx
plus_di = dmi.plusDI
minus_di = dmi.minusDI
```

Do not ask an `ADX` object for `.plusDI`; use `DMI` when the directional lines are required.

<a id="c-07"></a>
## C-07. Canonical strategy examples

The examples below carry descriptive class names for readability. **In a deliverable strategy file, the final class MUST be named `Strategy`** - either rename it directly (`class Strategy(bt.Strategy)`) or keep a helper base in the same file and ship `class Strategy(SingleOrderStrategy): ...`. The `SingleOrderStrategy` base from [C-04](#c-04) must then also be included in the same file (nothing is importable from elsewhere).

### EMA crossover - next-open execution

```python
import backtrader as bt


class EMACrossover(SingleOrderStrategy):
    params = dict(fast_period=20, slow_period=50)

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        if self.p.fast_period >= self.p.slow_period:
            raise ValueError("fast_period must be smaller than slow_period")
        self.fast = bt.ind.EMA(self.data.close, period=self.p.fast_period)
        self.slow = bt.ind.EMA(self.data.close, period=self.p.slow_period)
        self.cross = bt.ind.CrossOver(self.fast, self.slow)

    def next(self):
        if self.pending_order is not None:
            return
        if not self.position and self.cross[0] > 0:
            self.pending_order = self.buy()
        elif self.position and self.cross[0] < 0:
            self.pending_order = self.close()
```

This is the default standard implementation: indicators are declared once; a discrete crossover is used instead of `fast > slow` every bar; one order is allowed at a time; the close-derived signal fills no earlier than the next open.

### RSI mean reversion

```python
class RSIMeanReversion(SingleOrderStrategy):
    params = dict(period=14, entry=30.0, exit=50.0)

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        if not 0.0 <= self.p.entry < self.p.exit <= 100.0:
            raise ValueError("Require 0 <= entry < exit <= 100")
        self.rsi = bt.ind.RSI_Safe(self.data.close, period=self.p.period)

    def next(self):
        if self.pending_order is not None:
            return
        if not self.position and self.rsi[0] < self.p.entry:
            self.pending_order = self.buy()
        elif self.position and self.rsi[0] > self.p.exit:
            self.pending_order = self.close()
```

### MACD crossover

```python
class MACDCrossover(SingleOrderStrategy):
    params = dict(fast=12, slow=26, signal=9)

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.macd = bt.ind.MACDHisto(
            self.data.close,
            period_me1=self.p.fast,
            period_me2=self.p.slow,
            period_signal=self.p.signal,
            movav=bt.ind.EMA,
        )
        self.cross = bt.ind.CrossOver(self.macd.macd, self.macd.signal)

    def next(self):
        if self.pending_order is not None:
            return
        if not self.position and self.cross[0] > 0:
            self.pending_order = self.buy()
        elif self.position and self.cross[0] < 0:
            self.pending_order = self.close()
```

### Bollinger mean reversion

```python
class BollingerMeanReversion(SingleOrderStrategy):
    params = dict(period=20, deviations=2.0)

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.bb = bt.ind.BollingerBands(
            self.data.close,
            period=self.p.period,
            devfactor=self.p.deviations,
            movav=bt.ind.SMA,
        )
        self.enter = bt.ind.CrossDown(self.data.close, self.bb.bot)
        self.exit = bt.ind.CrossUp(self.data.close, self.bb.mid)

    def next(self):
        if self.pending_order is not None:
            return
        if not self.position and self.enter[0] > 0:
            self.pending_order = self.buy()
        elif self.position and self.exit[0] > 0:
            self.pending_order = self.close()
```

<a id="c-08"></a>
## C-08. Order types and fill semantics

Standard strategy methods include `buy`, `sell`, `close`, `buy_bracket`, `sell_bracket`, `order_target_size`, `order_target_value`, and `order_target_percent`.

| Backtrader order | Typical use | Key behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `bt.Order.Market` | Enter/exit at next available market | Normally next bar open |
| `bt.Order.Close` | Execute at session/bar close | Uses the next close execution convention |
| `bt.Order.Limit` | Buy no higher / sell no lower than limit | Can receive price improvement based on bar matching |
| `bt.Order.Stop` | Trigger then become market | Gap may produce a worse fill |
| `bt.Order.StopLimit` | Trigger then become limit | May trigger and remain unfilled |
| `bt.Order.StopTrail` | Trailing stop | Trail amount or percentage |
| `bt.Order.StopTrailLimit` | Trailing trigger with limit | Can remain unfilled after trigger |

Examples:

```python
market = self.buy(size=10)
limit = self.buy(size=10, exectype=bt.Order.Limit, price=99.50)
stop = self.sell(size=10, exectype=bt.Order.Stop, price=95.00)
stop_limit = self.buy(
    size=10,
    exectype=bt.Order.StopLimit,
    price=105.00,   # trigger
    plimit=105.25,  # limit after trigger
)
trail = self.sell(size=10, exectype=bt.Order.StopTrail, trailpercent=0.05)
```

The standard historical broker matches against OHLC and normally ignores volume. It is not an order-book simulator. Do not promise partial fills or queue priority unless a custom broker/filler explicitly implements them.

### Bracket order

```python
parent, stop, target = self.buy_bracket(
    size=10,
    exectype=bt.Order.Market,
    stopprice=95.0,
    stopexec=bt.Order.Stop,
    limitprice=110.0,
    limitexec=bt.Order.Limit,
)
```

A bracket consists of a parent and two linked children. Children activate only after the parent completes; execution of one child cancels the other. Prices should be based on a realizable reference. When stop/target distances must be based on the actual entry fill, submit children from `notify_order` after the parent completes rather than guessing the fill price in advance.

### OCO

```python
stop_order = self.sell(size=10, exectype=bt.Order.Stop, price=95.0)
target_order = self.sell(
    size=10,
    exectype=bt.Order.Limit,
    price=110.0,
    oco=stop_order,
)
```

Track both order references. A cancel notification for the sibling is expected after one completes.

### `cheat_on_open` - NOT available in BacktestLoop

`cheat_on_open` requires Cerebro-level configuration, and the platform runner does not enable it. Do not write `next_open()` methods or logic that assumes open-phase decision-making - it will silently never run. The standard event cycle (signal on bar `t`, market fill at open of `t+1`) always applies.

<a id="c-09"></a>
## C-09. Position sizing and risk

### Fixed units

```python
self.buy(size=100)
```

### Target percent

```python
self.order_target_percent(target=0.50)  # target 50% of portfolio value
self.order_target_percent(target=0.00)  # flatten
```

### Volatility-risk sizing

For a long entry with initial stop `m * ATR` below the fill:

```text
cash_risk = portfolio_value * risk_fraction
risk_per_unit = ATR * stop_multiple * contract_multiplier
units = floor(cash_risk / risk_per_unit)
```

A robust example that installs stop/target orders from the actual fill:

```python
import math
import backtrader as bt


class ATRRiskManagedLong(bt.Strategy):
    params = dict(
        ema_period=50,
        atr_period=14,
        risk_fraction=0.01,
        stop_atr=2.0,
        target_atr=4.0,
        contract_multiplier=1.0,
    )

    def __init__(self):
        self.ema = bt.ind.EMA(self.data.close, period=self.p.ema_period)
        self.atr = bt.ind.ATR(self.data, period=self.p.atr_period)
        self.entry_order = None
        self.stop_order = None
        self.target_order = None
        self.entry_atr = None

    def next(self):
        if any(order is not None for order in (self.entry_order, self.stop_order, self.target_order)):
            return
        if self.position:
            return
        if self.data.close[0] <= self.ema[0]:
            return

        risk_per_unit = self.atr[0] * self.p.stop_atr * self.p.contract_multiplier
        if not math.isfinite(risk_per_unit) or risk_per_unit <= 0:
            return
        cash_risk = self.broker.getvalue() * self.p.risk_fraction
        size = math.floor(cash_risk / risk_per_unit)
        if size <= 0:
            return

        self.entry_atr = float(self.atr[0])
        self.entry_order = self.buy(size=size)

    def notify_order(self, order):
        if order.status in (order.Submitted, order.Accepted):
            return

        if self.entry_order is not None and order.ref == self.entry_order.ref:
            if order.status == order.Completed:
                fill = order.executed.price
                size = abs(order.executed.size)
                stop_price = fill - self.p.stop_atr * self.entry_atr
                target_price = fill + self.p.target_atr * self.entry_atr
                self.stop_order = self.sell(
                    size=size,
                    exectype=bt.Order.Stop,
                    price=stop_price,
                )
                self.target_order = self.sell(
                    size=size,
                    exectype=bt.Order.Limit,
                    price=target_price,
                    oco=self.stop_order,
                )
            self.entry_order = None
            return

        if self.stop_order is not None and order.ref == self.stop_order.ref:
            if order.status in (order.Completed, order.Canceled, order.Margin, order.Rejected, order.Expired):
                self.stop_order = None
        if self.target_order is not None and order.ref == self.target_order.ref:
            if order.status in (order.Completed, order.Canceled, order.Margin, order.Rejected, order.Expired):
                self.target_order = None
```

For futures, remember the per-point dollar value is the contract multiplier - size in whole contracts and let the platform's broker fee model apply multiplier, margin, and commission. For FX, size in units/lots as the fee model expects; a generic stock sizing formula is not sufficient.

**Platform default sizing rule:** when the user specifies no sizing, default to **percent-of-equity** (~95% of equity per position for single-asset long-only strategies, or 1-2% risk-per-trade when a stop loss exists) so results read as portfolio returns rather than a handful of dollars. State the sizing assumption in one line when presenting results, and lead metric reporting with **return %**, not absolute $ P&L. Never place orders without an explicit `size`/`target`.

<a id="c-10"></a>
## C-10. Commission and slippage - platform-owned

Costs come from the platform's **broker fee model** for the job's symbol/asset class (real venues: Alpaca-style equity commission, per-contract futures fees with margin and multiplier, crypto/forex spread models). The runner passes them to `broker.setcommission(...)` itself. Consequences for the strategy author:

- **Never** call `cerebro.broker.setcommission(...)` or `set_slippage_*` - there is no `cerebro` in scope, and inventing cost numbers would double-charge or contradict the seeded fee model.
- **Never** pick or invent a fee model in code. The platform resolves the per-asset-class default; the job's `broker_fee_model` parameter changes it.
- Sizing math MAY assume the fee model's structure qualitatively (futures margin per contract, contract multiplier for per-point dollar value) - the broker applies the exact numbers.
- Order rejections for insufficient cash/margin surface via `notify_order` with `order.Margin` status - handle them (clear the pending-order slot; optionally log) instead of ignoring them.

<a id="c-11"></a>
## C-11. Data feeds - injected by the platform, never constructed

The strategy never constructs feeds. The platform's market-data layer downloads all bars (the strategy has no data-acquisition role at all) and the runner attaches one feed per job source:

- The **primary** feed comes from the job's symbol/timeframe parameters.
- Each **additional source** (the job's `additionalSources`) becomes another feed.
- Every feed is named `{SYMBOL}_{TIMEFRAME}` (e.g. `AAPL_1d`, `NVDA_1h`, `SPY_5m`).

Access patterns inside the strategy:

```python
self.data                      # first feed (fine for single-feed jobs)
self.datas                     # all feeds
self.getdatanames()            # list of feed names
self.getdatabyname("AAPL_1d")  # fetch a specific feed by name (preferred in multi-feed jobs)
d._name                        # a feed's name
```

Standard lines on every feed: `open`, `high`, `low`, `close`, `volume`. Custom data lines (sentiment feeds, alternative data) are not part of the platform data contract - if such logic is needed, derive it inside the strategy from the price feeds or job params rather than expecting extra feed columns.

<a id="c-12"></a>
## C-12. Multiple assets and timeframes

Multi-asset and multi-timeframe jobs are configured through the job's `additionalSources` - the platform injects one feed per source, named `{SYMBOL}_{TIMEFRAME}`. There is no `cerebro.resampledata` in strategy code; a higher timeframe is simply another injected feed (e.g. primary `AAPL_1m` plus additional `AAPL_1d`).

Core rules (must follow):

1. **Never assume `self.data`/`self.datas[0]` is "primary" in multi-source jobs** - feed ordering can vary. Target feeds by **name** (`self.getdatabyname(...)`), with names carried in strategy params (`primary_name`, `htf_name`, ...) so they stay overridable.
2. **Orders and positions are per-feed:** `self.buy(data=d, ...)`, `self.close(data=d)`, `self.getposition(d)`. Avoid the `self.position` shorthand except in single-feed strategies.
3. **Track pending orders per feed** (`self.orders = {d: None for d in self.datas}`; clear in `notify_order` via `order.data`).
4. **Higher-timeframe feeds do not advance every `next()`.** Detect a new HTF bar via a `len(htf)` change and update HTF state only then; execute on the lower timeframe.

### Multiple assets - trade every feed independently

```python
class MultiAssetTrend(bt.Strategy):
    params = dict(period=50)

    def __init__(self):
        self.ema = {data: bt.ind.EMA(data.close, period=self.p.period) for data in self.datas}
        self.pending = {data: None for data in self.datas}

    def next(self):
        for data in self.datas:
            if self.pending[data] is not None:
                continue
            position = self.getposition(data)
            if not position and data.close[0] > self.ema[data][0]:
                self.pending[data] = self.buy(data=data)
            elif position and data.close[0] < self.ema[data][0]:
                self.pending[data] = self.close(data=data)

    def notify_order(self, order):
        if order.status in (order.Submitted, order.Accepted):
            return
        self.pending[order.data] = None
```

### Higher-timeframe filter + lower-timeframe execution

```python
class Strategy(bt.Strategy):
    params = dict(ltf_name="AAPL_1m", htf_name="AAPL_1d", fast=10, slow=30, size=1)

    def __init__(self):
        self.ltf = self.getdatabyname(self.p.ltf_name)
        self.htf = self.getdatabyname(self.p.htf_name)

        self.htf_sma = bt.ind.SMA(self.htf.close, period=50)
        self.ltf_fast = bt.ind.EMA(self.ltf.close, period=self.p.fast)
        self.ltf_slow = bt.ind.EMA(self.ltf.close, period=self.p.slow)
        self.ltf_x = bt.ind.CrossOver(self.ltf_fast, self.ltf_slow)

        self.orders = {self.ltf: None, self.htf: None}
        self._last_htf_len = len(self.htf)
        self.htf_trend_up = False

    def notify_order(self, order):
        if order.status in (order.Completed, order.Canceled, order.Margin, order.Rejected):
            self.orders[order.data] = None

    def next(self):
        # Update HTF state only when the HTF bar advances
        if len(self.htf) != self._last_htf_len:
            self._last_htf_len = len(self.htf)
            self.htf_trend_up = self.htf.close[0] > self.htf_sma[0]

        if self.orders[self.ltf]:
            return
        pos = self.getposition(self.ltf)
        if not pos and self.htf_trend_up and self.ltf_x[0] > 0:
            self.orders[self.ltf] = self.buy(data=self.ltf, size=self.p.size)
        elif pos and (not self.htf_trend_up or self.ltf_x[0] < 0):
            self.orders[self.ltf] = self.close(data=self.ltf)
```

A higher-timeframe bar must be completed before its close can be used - the injected HTF feed already delivers only completed bars, and the `len(htf)` gate above uses each daily value only from the moment it exists. Do not manually backfill a day's final close into earlier intraday bars.

<a id="c-13"></a>
## C-13. Custom indicator patterns

### Pattern 1: declarative line graph - preferred

Use existing line operations whenever possible. Backtrader can optimize these through its normal `next`/`once` machinery.

```python
class ZScore(bt.Indicator):
    lines = ("zscore",)
    params = (("period", 20),)

    def __init__(self):
        mean = bt.ind.SMA(self.data, period=self.p.period)
        std = bt.ind.StdDev(self.data, period=self.p.period)
        self.l.zscore = bt.DivByZero(self.data - mean, std, float("nan"))
        super().__init__()
```

### Pattern 2: stateful `next` implementation

Use this when output genuinely depends on prior output state. Requirements:

- declare output `lines` and parameters;
- ensure an adequate minimum period;
- initialize in `nextstart` or handle the first bar explicitly;
- derive current output from current inputs and prior line values;
- remain idempotent if the same bar is recalculated in replay/live mode;
- avoid increment-only hidden counters unless they are keyed by timestamp and update-safe.

### Pattern 3: optimized `once`

A custom `once(start, end)` MAY be added for batch speed. It must produce the same values as `next`. Correctness comes first; do not write a fragile `once` implementation merely to appear optimized.

<a id="c-14"></a>
## C-14. Tested custom Backtrader indicators

### On-Balance Volume

```python
class OnBalanceVolume(bt.Indicator):
    lines = ("obv",)
    plotinfo = dict(subplot=True)

    def nextstart(self):
        self.l.obv[0] = self.data.volume[0]

    def next(self):
        if self.data.close[0] > self.data.close[-1]:
            self.l.obv[0] = self.l.obv[-1] + self.data.volume[0]
        elif self.data.close[0] < self.data.close[-1]:
            self.l.obv[0] = self.l.obv[-1] - self.data.volume[0]
        else:
            self.l.obv[0] = self.l.obv[-1]
```

This matches the `BTL_CANONICAL_V1` first-value convention. Another library may seed OBV at zero; record the convention when comparing outputs.

### Rolling VWAP

```python
class RollingVWAP(bt.Indicator):
    lines = ("vwap",)
    params = (("period", 20),)
    plotinfo = dict(subplot=False)

    def __init__(self):
        typical = (self.data.high + self.data.low + self.data.close) / 3.0
        pv_sum = bt.ind.SumN(typical * self.data.volume, period=self.p.period)
        volume_sum = bt.ind.SumN(self.data.volume, period=self.p.period)
        self.l.vwap = bt.DivByZero(pv_sum, volume_sum, float("nan"))
        super().__init__()
```

### Session VWAP

```python
class SessionVWAP(bt.Indicator):
    lines = ("vwap", "cum_pv", "cum_volume")
    plotinfo = dict(subplot=False)
    plotlines = dict(
        cum_pv=dict(_plotskip=True),
        cum_volume=dict(_plotskip=True),
    )

    def _bar_values(self):
        typical = (self.data.high[0] + self.data.low[0] + self.data.close[0]) / 3.0
        volume = self.data.volume[0]
        return typical * volume, volume

    def nextstart(self):
        pv, volume = self._bar_values()
        self.l.cum_pv[0] = pv
        self.l.cum_volume[0] = volume
        self.l.vwap[0] = pv / volume if volume else float("nan")

    def next(self):
        pv, volume = self._bar_values()
        new_session = self.data.datetime.date(0) != self.data.datetime.date(-1)
        if new_session:
            cum_pv, cum_volume = pv, volume
        else:
            cum_pv = self.l.cum_pv[-1] + pv
            cum_volume = self.l.cum_volume[-1] + volume
        self.l.cum_pv[0] = cum_pv
        self.l.cum_volume[0] = cum_volume
        self.l.vwap[0] = cum_pv / cum_volume if cum_volume else float("nan")
```

This sample resets at the calendar date in the feed timezone. Exchange sessions that cross midnight or have custom opens require an explicit session identifier line rather than `date()`.

### Prior-bar Donchian channel

```python
class DonchianChannel(bt.Indicator):
    lines = ("upper", "lower", "mid")
    params = (("period", 20), ("lookback", -1))
    plotinfo = dict(subplot=False)

    def __init__(self):
        prior_high = self.data.high(self.p.lookback)
        prior_low = self.data.low(self.p.lookback)
        self.l.upper = bt.ind.Highest(prior_high, period=self.p.period)
        self.l.lower = bt.ind.Lowest(prior_low, period=self.p.period)
        self.l.mid = (self.l.upper + self.l.lower) / 2.0
        super().__init__()
```

### Donchian breakout strategy

```python
class DonchianBreakout(SingleOrderStrategy):
    params = dict(entry_period=20, exit_period=10)

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.entry_channel = DonchianChannel(self.data, period=self.p.entry_period)
        self.exit_channel = DonchianChannel(self.data, period=self.p.exit_period)

    def next(self):
        if self.pending_order is not None:
            return
        if not self.position and self.data.close[0] > self.entry_channel.upper[0]:
            self.pending_order = self.buy()
        elif self.position and self.data.close[0] < self.exit_channel.lower[0]:
            self.pending_order = self.close()
```

### Supertrend with canonical Wilder ATR

```python
class SuperTrend(bt.Indicator):
    lines = ("supertrend", "direction", "final_upper", "final_lower")
    params = (("period", 10), ("multiplier", 3.0))
    plotinfo = dict(subplot=False)
    plotlines = dict(
        direction=dict(_plotskip=True),
        final_upper=dict(_plotskip=True),
        final_lower=dict(_plotskip=True),
    )

    def __init__(self):
        atr = bt.ind.ATR(self.data, period=self.p.period)
        hl2 = (self.data.high + self.data.low) / 2.0
        self._basic_upper = hl2 + self.p.multiplier * atr
        self._basic_lower = hl2 - self.p.multiplier * atr
        super().__init__()

    def nextstart(self):
        upper = self._basic_upper[0]
        lower = self._basic_lower[0]
        self.l.final_upper[0] = upper
        self.l.final_lower[0] = lower
        if self.data.close[0] <= upper:
            self.l.supertrend[0] = upper
            self.l.direction[0] = -1.0
        else:
            self.l.supertrend[0] = lower
            self.l.direction[0] = 1.0

    def next(self):
        basic_upper = self._basic_upper[0]
        basic_lower = self._basic_lower[0]
        previous_upper = self.l.final_upper[-1]
        previous_lower = self.l.final_lower[-1]
        previous_close = self.data.close[-1]

        final_upper = (
            basic_upper
            if basic_upper < previous_upper or previous_close > previous_upper
            else previous_upper
        )
        final_lower = (
            basic_lower
            if basic_lower > previous_lower or previous_close < previous_lower
            else previous_lower
        )
        self.l.final_upper[0] = final_upper
        self.l.final_lower[0] = final_lower

        previous_supertrend = self.l.supertrend[-1]
        if previous_supertrend == previous_upper:
            current = final_upper if self.data.close[0] <= final_upper else final_lower
        else:
            current = final_lower if self.data.close[0] >= final_lower else final_upper

        self.l.supertrend[0] = current
        self.l.direction[0] = 1.0 if self.data.close[0] > current else -1.0
```

This implementation is idempotent because each current value is derived from current inputs and completed prior-line values, not from a hidden mutable accumulator.

<a id="c-15"></a>
## C-15. Optional TA-Lib integration

When the Python TA-Lib package and native library are installed, Backtrader dynamically exposes TA-Lib functions under `bt.talib`. This is optional capability, not a core guarantee.

```python
import backtrader as bt


def require_bt_talib(name: str):
    candidate = getattr(bt.talib, name, None)
    if candidate is None:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"TA-Lib indicator {name!r} is unavailable. "
            "Install/verify TA-Lib or use a documented custom implementation."
        )
    return candidate


TALIB_OBV = require_bt_talib("OBV")
```

TA-Lib input order, defaults, unstable periods, seed behavior, and output names may differ from Backtrader-native indicators. Do not mix implementations inside one optimization without recording the source.

<a id="c-16"></a>
## C-16. Analyzers, optimization, and reproducibility - platform-owned

**Analyzers:** the runner attaches the platform's own analyzer set (equity curve, Sharpe, returns, drawdown, trade list, order record) and extracts results into the shared cross-engine format the frontend renders. Do not add analyzers in strategy code.

**Parameter optimization:** never `cerebro.optstrategy` - there is no `cerebro`. Parameter sweeps and A/B variations run through the platform's **experiments** feature (`run_experiments`), which executes variations against the job without changing it: parameter overrides map onto the `Strategy.params` / `params` dict, and code variations use file overrides. This is why every tunable value MUST live in `params` rather than being inlined. Filter logically invalid combinations (e.g. `fast >= slow`) before proposing a sweep.

**Reproducibility:** for stochastic logic, set and record seeds (`random.seed(42)`, `np.random.seed(42)`) at module level in the strategy file. Deterministic indicator code does not make Monte Carlo or ML pipelines deterministic automatically.

<a id="c-17"></a>
## C-17. Backtrader gotchas and repair map

| Symptom | Likely cause | Correct repair |
|---|---|---|
| `AttributeError: ... indicators has no attribute X` | Invented or wrong alias | Resolve exact registry; use optional TA-Lib/custom implementation |
| `AttributeError` on `.upper` or `.hist` | Wrong output line name | Inspect `lines.getlinealiases()`; e.g. Bollinger `.top`, MACDHisto `.histo` |
| `ZeroDivisionError` in RSI | Bare RSI on flat data | Use `RSI_Safe` or define safe division convention |
| Strategy enters every bar | Level condition used without position/order guard | Add position state, pending-order guard, or crossover event |
| Duplicate orders | `buy()` called while previous order pending | Track order references until terminal notification |
| Entry appears one bar late | Expected same-close fill | This IS the correct next-open behavior (both engines); same-close exists only as the executionTiming escape hatch |
| Unrealistically good fill | Lookahead in signal logic | Inspect the signal-to-fill timeline; costs are already applied by the platform broker fee model |
| Custom indicator differs in `runonce=True` | `next`/`once` mismatch | Remove or fix `once`; add fixture parity test |
| Replay/live output changes on repeated bar | Hidden mutable state is not idempotent | Compute current state from prior lines and current inputs |
| Multi-data strategy reads wrong position | Used `self.position` | Use `self.getposition(data)` |
| Higher-timeframe lookahead | Higher-timeframe close used before its bar completed | Gate HTF state on `len(htf)` advancing (C-12); no backward fill |
| Order never fills | Limit/stop constraints, cash/margin, or status ignored | Inspect `notify_order`, OHLC matching, validity, and broker cash |
| `and/or` error in `__init__` | Python Boolean operators on line objects | Use `bt.And`, `bt.Or`, or move concrete logic to `next` |
